title: UPC Controlled Vocabularies
description: Single source of truth for every closed enum in the Universal Provenance Corpus standard. Object schemas $ref these definitions (e.g. "vocab.json#/$defs/confidence") so terminology is defined in exactly one place. Extensible fields anyOf a closed enum with an "x-" prefixed escape hatch.

interpretation.description: How directly the source supports an extracted statement.

confidence.description: Qualitative confidence. pi-forge stores this enum; RA stores a float. Use this field for the enum and confidence_score for the float; either or both may be present.

confidence_score.description: Optional numeric confidence in [0,1]. Present when a tool computes a numeric score.

status.description: Terminal outcome of an activity or object stage.

extraction_status.description: Lifecycle state of an extraction. Only `active` extractions are gated (§03) and exported; the others are retained and surfaced so nothing is lost. Defaults to active when absent.

fetch_status.description: Richer acquisition outcome for a source representation.

source_kind.description: The primary nature of a source, independent of its representations.

representation_role.description: What a representation IS relative to its source. A source may have many representations; role classifies each. Native PDFs are document_pdf (preserved as PDF); a print-to-PDF of a web page is rendered_pdf.

extraction_type.description: The kind of evidence an extraction represents. Closed base vocabulary (pi-forge literature vocab + RA in-text citation) plus an x- escape hatch for tool-specific types.

locator_type.description: How a locator points into a representation. The value shape depends on the type (see locator.schema.json).

activity_type.description: A recorded step in the provenance/events.jsonl journal. Production steps plus the correction/removal steps (modify, reanchor, retract, remove, redact) that make the journal an audit and removal log (§07, §10).

field_origin.description: Where a bibliographic field value came from (field-level provenance). Generalizes RA CitationFieldEvidence.source_type and pi-forge document-ingest field origin.

produced_by_method.description: The deterministic or model method that produced a representation or derived object. Closed base vocabulary plus an x- escape hatch for tool-specific methods (e.g. x-yt-dlp).

identifier_scheme.description: Recommended scheme for a source-level external identifier (source.identifiers[].scheme). Advisory only: an unrecognized non-x- scheme raises the advisory identifier_scheme_unknown (§08), never a hard error, and UPC never resolves the identifier against any external registry (§06). Closed base list plus an x- escape hatch for tool- or domain-specific schemes. Note: source.identifiers[].scheme is a free string in the schema (so an unlisted scheme is advisory, not schema-invalid); this vocabulary is the registry the advisory consults.

relation_type.description: Typed relationship from a source to another work (source.relations[].type). The intra-corpus supersession chain remains carried by the top-level scalar supersedes/superseded_by fields (which drive the cites_superseded conformance rule); relations[] of type supersedes/superseded_by are advisory metadata, typically to an external work, and never substitute for those scalar fields (§02). Closed base vocabulary plus an x- escape hatch.
